content.title: American Idol: How to vote for your favorites in Season 24
content.text: American Idol has gone through several facelifts during this 24th season, including a shortened Hollywood Week (in Nashville, no less) and a special 'Ohana Round in Hawaii (featuring music influencers). But now that ABC's reality competition is entering the live shows, there's a new wrinkle that all Idol fans should be aware of: the voting has changed. Utilized in prior seasons, the official American Idol app was discontinued this year, and voting now occurs in one of three ways: on the show's website, via text message, and on social media. It's the social media angle that's causing some confusion among Idol viewers. For your social media vote to count, you must comment on the pinned official voting post for the night on Facebook, Instagram, and TikTok — and only when voting is open. But, of course, there is fine print. Specifically, you must spell the contestant's name correctly, you can't reply to someone else's post, and you can't list more than one name. Here are the error messages fans receive if they break any of those rules: MISSPELLING ERROR: "This isn't getting pulled in as an official vote due to the misspelling. Please make sure you're spelling the name correctly as it appears in the graphic of this post." REPLY ERROR: "Votes done as a reply to a comment do not count. To submit your vote, please do a fresh comment that is not a reply." LIST ERROR: "This counts as a vote for Keyla only. If you want to vote for Madison, Rae, Jordan, Philmon, Lucas, Chris, and Julian, please submit additional new comments with their names." From now until the end of the season, American Idol airs live Mondays at 8 p.m. on ABC, streams live on Disney+, and also streams the next day on Hulu. The first live show on March 30 welcomes back the Top 20 artists to perform "Songs of Faith." Luke Bryan and Lionel Richie will open the show with a performance of "Jesus Is Love" alongside the Top 20, while Carrie Underwood will perform "How Great Thou Art" with last season's three platinum ticket winners Filo Ebid, Kolbi Jordan, and Canaan James Hill. Only 12 of the Top 20 artists will advance to the next round. The current contestants are: Makiyah, Jake Thistle, Genevieve Hayward, Daniel Stallworth, Kyndal Inskeep, Kutter Bradley, Jesse Findling, Hannah Harper, Braden Rumfelt, Brooks, Philmon Lee, Rae, Lucas Leon, Jordan McCollough, Abayomi, Madison Moon, Chris Tungseth, Ruby Rae, Julián Kalel, and Keyla Richardson. Sound off in the comments and predict the Season 24 winner — and weekly eliminations — in Gold Derby's predictions center.
